sources.title: Jan Zur, Matrix Functions, TU Berlin full lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 101-page PDF inspected. §§2.2, 2.4–2.6, PDF pp. 13–26, Jordan derivative formula, Cauchy definition, equivalence and primary versus non-primary convention; §3.2.1–3.2.3, pp. 34–42, principal logarithm/square-root branches and their spectral domains; §4.1–4.1.1, pp. 51–56, Fréchet derivative definition and block identity; §5.2–5.2.3, pp. 64–71, Parlett and block Parlett recurrences, disjoint spectra and clustering; §5.3.1, pp. 73–74, Newton sign iteration and convergence; §5.4.1–5.4.2, pp. 85–91, diagonal Padé approximants and scaling-and-squaring.
sources.support: Independent full lecture-note treatment. The notes state the Jordan, contour and block-recurrence formulas; their cited proof gaps for some results are completed in the local carriers. Their floating-point algorithm is context only: the authored claims use a finite scalar Padé bound, explicit contour resolvent hypotheses, exact Sylvester certificates, and explicit inconclusive branches.

contents.name: §§2.2, 2.4–2.6: Jordan-block derivatives, contour definition and equivalence, primary-branch convention
contents.support: The local theorem proves the resolvent expansion on each Jordan block, applies the scalar Cauchy derivative formula entrywise, establishes independence using Hermite interpolation and Jordan similarity, and matches the published normal spectral calculus.

contents.name: §§3.2.1–3.2.3: principal scalar branch cuts and the principal matrix square-root/logarithm domain
contents.support: The local proof uses the existing principal scalar branch items and proves the matrix logarithm identity and the principal square-root branch, including the Sylvester uniqueness argument for roots with spectrum in the right half-plane.

contents.name: §§4.1–4.1.1: Fréchet derivative definition and block upper-triangular function identity
contents.support: The notes state the block identity but cite an external proof. The authored theorem supplies a full proof from the primary contour formula and a separate power-series derivation of the exponential integral.

contents.name: §§5.2–5.2.3: Schur-Parlett recurrence, Sylvester separation and merging/cluster caveats
contents.support: The block recurrence is used with the exact sign convention (T_{ii}F_{ij}-F_{ij}T_{jj}); the local definition specifies exact Schur certificates, bounded merging, a finite Jordan-data diagonal evaluator, exact Sylvester solves and inconclusive outcomes. No numerical stability theorem is inferred.

contents.name: §5.3.1: Newton iteration (X_{k+1}=(X_k+X_k^{-1})/2) for the matrix sign and its convergence proof
contents.support: The local proof gives the commuting-factor identity, the squared Cayley-transform recurrence, convergence from spectral radius less than one, and the explicit quadratic norm inequality.

contents.name: §§5.4.1–5.4.2: diagonal Padé coefficients and scaling-and-squaring method
contents.support: The source fixes the (r_m(2^{-s}A)^{2^s}) structure. The authored carriers provide their own explicit scalar remainder and squaring-error proofs, and do not claim Higham's adaptive parameter choices.

contents.name: §§2.2, 2.4–2.6: Jordan block formula and common scalar branch
contents.support: The local definition fixes one branch across all Jordan blocks; its well-definedness is proved separately.

contents.name: §§2.2, 2.4–2.6: finite Hermite interpolation at the eigenvalue data
contents.support: The local lemma proves injectivity and surjectivity for the finite derivative map, including the empty-data case.

contents.name: §§5.4.1–5.4.2: diagonal Padé coefficients and rational exponential approximant
contents.support: The local definition fixes the coefficient normalization and denominator-zero convention.

contents.name: §§5.4.1–5.4.2: scalar Padé remainder representation
contents.support: The local lemma derives its finite disk bound from the exact beta-integral identity; no adaptive parameter rule is imported.

contents.name: §§5.4.1–5.4.2: repeated squaring in exponential evaluation
contents.support: The local lemma proves the noncommutative defect recurrence directly.

contents.name: §§2.4–2.6 and §5.4.1–5.4.2: Cauchy representation used to transfer scalar error
contents.support: The local theorem proves the contour norm transfer and keeps the uniform resolvent hypothesis explicit.

contents.name: §§5.4.1–5.4.2: scalar approximation error propagated through repeated squaring
contents.support: The local theorem gives a conditional finite bound and does not import an adaptive Higham choice.

contents.name: §§5.2.1–5.2.4: Parlett block recurrence and separated Sylvester solves
contents.support: The local proof establishes exact reconstruction from the block recurrence and its unique solves.

contents.name: §§3.2.1–3.2.3: principal branches for matrix logarithm and square root
contents.support: The local algorithm checks the branch domain and returns explicit inconclusive statuses.

contents.name: §5.3.1: scalar sign branch on the two open half-planes
contents.support: The local definition applies this branch through the primary matrix calculus.

contents.name: §5.3.1: finite Newton update for the matrix sign
contents.support: The local procedure has finite-budget and solve-failure statuses; it makes no rounded convergence claim.
